meta.note: Ubiquitous-language ontology for this repo's domain: the vocabulary the code embodies, and the explicit typed relations between terms (is-a, part-of, relates, persists, references, describes, determines). Deliberately separate from concept_store/concepts.json -- that store is architecture PER MODULE (one summary per file) and answers 'what does this module promise'. This file is vocabulary PER DOMAIN TERM and answers 'what is this thing, and what is it to the others' -- a term here can span several modules (SessionState alone is written and read by nearly every node in the graph), and a module can define several terms, so it does not fit concept_store's per-file shape. Ground truth is still the code; this is a durable, human-readable map of the graph rather than N separate summaries. Modelled on task-framework/ontology/task-domain.json: definitions describe what a term IS in domain vocabulary, not how it's implemented -- evidence is a single pointer, a hint for verification, not an implementation trail.

bounded_contexts.Hook Dispatch: The raw Claude Code hook event surface: reading stdin JSON, POSTing it to the FastAPI server, and routing each event type (UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionStart, SessionEnd) to its handler. Concerned with getting the payload from Claude Code's process to the right handler function -- not with what that handler decides.
bounded_contexts.Gates/Enforcement: The anti-hallucination send-gate system: verifying a tool call against session history before it is allowed to execute, and the separate commit-traceability check that every git commit references a task id. Fails open on any internal error -- a gate that can't evaluate never blocks the call.
bounded_contexts.Session & Checkpoint State: The SessionState schema and its persistence: one checkpoint per session, the public entry points that read/invoke/write it, and the bookkeeping (checkpoint trim, live-session audit) needed to keep an in-memory, non-persistent store from growing unboundedly.
bounded_contexts.LangGraph Node Pipeline: The node callables that actually do work inside the compiled session graph -- one class per file, wired together into event chains and looked up by name through a registry. Distinct from Session & Checkpoint State: this context is the node implementations and their structural contracts, not the state they read and write.
bounded_contexts.Memory & Retrieval: Scoring and injecting relevant memories and tool hints into a turn via cheap keyword-overlap signals (no embeddings). Defines the seam that lets nodes swap in a null implementation for tests without touching the production scoring code.
bounded_contexts.Observability: Answering 'what happened, and what was I working on' after the fact: the consolidated cross-session event timeline, the raw log sink every module writes through, and the MCP tools that expose both for querying.
bounded_contexts.Concept Store: The per-module architectural-fact store this repo maintains about its own source, and about which repo boundary a piece of evidence is allowed to cross.
bounded_contexts.MCP Tool Surface: The tool registry claude-hooks exposes to callers: mapping domain names to modules, generating one tool per action, and the separate personal tool->domain/tool->skill lookup used by the pipeline to describe tool calls generically.

HookDispatchTable.definition: The lookup from each Claude Code hook event name to its handler. Single entry point for every hook event this repo processes.

HookClient.definition: The thin process Claude Code actually invokes per hook event: reads the hook payload and forwards it to HookServer, along with the real per-session cwd Claude Code already supplied -- never resolves or guesses it.

HookServer.definition: The persistent process HookClient talks to, replacing a slower per-invocation subprocess dispatcher. Owns the single checkpoint store for the whole server lifetime.

CopilotBridge.definition: A CLI-driven alternative to HookClient for non-Claude-Code callers (Copilot-oriented workflows, shell wrappers) that sends the same prompt/pre-tool/post-tool events to the same HookServer, without needing Claude Code's native hook payload format.

UserPromptSubmit.definition: The event fired when the user submits a prompt, before Claude sees it. The point where memories, active-task context, and other injected context get attached to the turn.

PreToolUse.definition: The moment just before any tool call executes -- machine-wide, across every MCP server and built-in tool, not scoped to this repo. The point where a call can still be denied.

PostToolUse.definition: The moment just after any tool call returns, machine-wide like PreToolUse. The point where a completed call is observed and recorded, never denied.

GateContext.definition: The dataclass a PreToolUse call is packaged into before a Gate evaluates it: tool name, tool input, the current prompt's tool calls so far, and recent prompt text. What a Gate actually sees -- it never touches SessionState directly.

Gate.definition: One send-gate rule: given a tool call and a GateContext, decide allow or deny with a reason. The commit-traceability check (every git commit references a task id) is the concrete example; other gates compose as chains.

GatePolicy.definition: The seam GateCheckNode dispatches through instead of calling gate logic directly, so a test can substitute a stub without the full gate machinery.

GateCheckNode.definition: The node PreToolUse routes to. Builds a GateContext from SessionState, dispatches to its GatePolicy, and fails open on any internal error -- a gate that cannot evaluate must never block the call it was supposed to check.

SessionState.definition: The single state shape every node in the session graph reads and returns a partial slice of. Carries routing, per-turn fields, and cross-turn fields side by side, though a given event only touches its own subset.

SessionGraph.definition: The single compiled graph handling all four hook event types via one topology, routed by event type. The one chokepoint every public entry point calls to reach the pipeline.

SessionCheckpoint.definition: One session's persisted SessionState, keyed by session id. In-memory only -- does not survive a server restart -- replacing a store that corrupted twice in production. Test sessions are isolated from the production store.

CheckpointTrim.definition: The cap on one session's checkpoint history, run on every Stop event. Exists because the in-memory store has no built-in eviction -- without it a long-running session's history grows unboundedly. Costs only time-travel to evicted checkpoints, never current-state correctness.

ActiveSessionLookup.definition: The only signal available for 'what session am I in' before any session id is explicitly known -- finds the single most-recently-written checkpoint across all sessions.

NodeCallable.definition: The structural contract every session-graph node satisfies: callable with a SessionState, returns a dict of partial state updates. What lets any registered node be instantiated uniformly regardless of which hook-event step it implements.

BackfillNodeProtocol.definition: The contract for the single pluggable memory-backfill slot in the UPS graph. Swapping strategies means replacing the graph edge, not subclassing -- multiple strategies must be composed inside one node rather than adding parallel backfill edges. Currently unwired -- the node that fed it was removed.

NodeRegistry.definition: The factory that turns a node name into a fresh NodeCallable instance for graph wiring. Enforces that every registered value is a class, never a pre-built instance shared across graphs.

McpHookBridgeNode.definition: The generic PostToolUse bridge: any MCP tool whose response carries a hook payload gets it piped into the turn's injected context, with no per-integration node needed.

NoopNode.definition: Routed to for stop events and unrecognised event types. Marks the first Stop of a turn, runs CheckpointTrim on every Stop, and logs a warning when more than one live session is detected -- surfacing forgotten detached sessions passively.

MemoryRetriever.definition: The seam LoadMemoriesNode dispatches through: given prompt tokens, return scored memory rows. The dependency arrow runs one way, nodes toward retrievers, never back.

ToolScorer.definition: The seam ScoreToolsNode dispatches through: given prompt keywords, return scored tool-hint rows. Usage count is only ever a tie-breaker on an existing keyword match, never enough on its own to manufacture relevance for an unrelated, frequently-called tool.

LoadMemoriesNode.definition: The UPS-chain node that tokenises the prompt, calls its MemoryRetriever, and records which memories surfaced and their hit counts -- recording is wrapped so a failure there degrades observability only, never the memories returned to the turn.

ServerMemory.definition: The two-layer consolidated cross-session event timeline answering 'what was I working on': prompts, tool calls, and task activations recorded as one chronological sequence, write-through so a read never has to reconcile the two layers.

SQLiteHandler.definition: The shared log handler every hook and pipeline module logs through. Singleton per DB path, redirects to an isolated test DB during tests. Auto-prunes to keep its table from growing without bound.

Concept.definition: A durable per-module architectural fact -- description, contracts, invariants, evidence -- keyed by module path. Evidence cites 'file:symbol' locations, never a bare line number (line numbers drift on every unrelated edit; symbol names mostly don't).

MCPToolMap.definition: The mapping from each domain name to its module and actions; registers one tool per action, named domain__action.

ToolDomainMap.definition: The personal tool-name -> domain/skill lookup, loaded from an external file. How the pipeline describes a raw MCP tool call in domain/skill terms without hardcoding every tool by name.

relations.subject: UserPromptSubmit
relations.note: One of the event names the table routes.

relations.subject: UserPromptSubmit
relations.note: The only event that reaches memory/tool retrieval -- there's nothing to inject before the prompt exists.

relations.subject: PreToolUse
relations.note: One of the event names the table routes.

relations.subject: PostToolUse
relations.note: PreToolUse's counterpart event, routed the same way.

relations.subject: PreToolUse
relations.note: The only event a Gate ever evaluates -- deny/allow only makes sense before the call happens.

relations.subject: PostToolUse
relations.note: The only node that inspects a tool's response after it returns.

relations.subject: UserPromptSubmit
relations.note: Sibling hook events in the same per-turn sequence: prompt, then zero or more tool calls each bracketed by PreToolUse/PostToolUse.

relations.subject: PreToolUse
relations.note: Before/after halves of the same tool call, machine-wide, not scoped to this repo's own tools.

relations.subject: HookClient
relations.note: HookClient forwards the stdin payload to HookServer; the two never share a process, only an HTTP contract.

relations.subject: CopilotBridge
relations.note: Functional analogue for non-Claude-Code callers -- same HookServer, same event vocabulary, different invocation surface (CLI args vs. stdin JSON from Claude Code itself).

relations.subject: HookDispatchTable
relations.note: The subprocess dispatch table and the FastAPI server's routes cover the same event set; the server is what HookClient actually talks to in production, the dispatcher remains for fallback/testing.

relations.subject: HookServer
relations.note: HookServer owns the one place a SessionCheckpoint's storage is constructed, for the life of the process.

relations.subject: SessionCheckpoint
relations.note: A checkpoint only exists as the persisted state of one session inside the graph's compiled store; it has no identity or storage independent of the graph that wrote it.

relations.subject: SessionState
relations.note: The shape that gets serialised into the checkpoint on every graph invoke; the checkpoint is 'a SessionState at time T for session X', not a separate schema.

relations.subject: CheckpointTrim
relations.note: A defensive, store-specific operation that deletes the oldest entries past a row cap for one session -- a no-op for any checkpointer with its own eviction.

relations.subject: ActiveSessionLookup
relations.note: Scans across all sessions' checkpoints for the most recently written one -- the only way to answer 'current session' before a session id is supplied, since no session identity exists outside the checkpoint store.

relations.subject: NodeCallable
relations.note: Every NodeCallable's contract is exactly 'takes a SessionState, returns a partial SessionState update' -- the contract is defined purely in terms of that one shared type.

relations.subject: NodeRegistry
relations.note: Not persistence in the storage sense -- NodeRegistry is the sole place fresh NodeCallable instances are constructed from, matching the analogous relation in ACME's and task-framework's ontologies for their own registries.

relations.subject: BackfillNodeProtocol
relations.note: A BackfillNodeProtocol implementor is still just a NodeCallable (same call signature); the extra protocol exists only to document the specific state fields the backfill slot is expected to read.

relations.subject: McpHookBridgeNode
relations.note: Structurally an ordinary PostToolUse node; its distinguishing behaviour (piping any tool's hook payload through generically) is a routing decision, not a different contract shape.

relations.subject: GateCheckNode
relations.note: Same NodeCallable contract as every other node; listed under Gates/Enforcement rather than LangGraph Node Pipeline because its behaviour (deny/allow via GatePolicy) is the point, not its place in the graph.

relations.subject: GateCheckNode
relations.note: Dispatches through the seam rather than calling gate logic directly, so tests can substitute a stub GatePolicy without touching the real gate machinery.

relations.subject: GatePolicy
relations.note: A GatePolicy's check always takes a GateContext as its argument; the seam's shape is defined in terms of that one type.

relations.subject: Gate
relations.note: Every concrete Gate receives a GateContext to decide against; a Gate never reads SessionState or the hook payload directly.

relations.subject: LoadMemoriesNode
relations.note: Accepts a MemoryRetriever at construction -- the node owns when retrieval happens, the retriever owns how memories are scored.

relations.subject: MemoryRetriever
relations.note: Sibling seams serving the same architectural role (swap production scoring for a null stub in tests) for two different data sources -- memory rows vs. tool-hint rows.

relations.subject: LoadMemoriesNode
relations.note: Records which memories surfaced after scoring, so it becomes part of the same cross-session timeline as prompts and tool calls -- a one-directional call, not a shared data structure.

relations.subject: ServerMemory
relations.note: Both write to the same database but through separate tables and separate write paths -- co-located storage, not a shared schema.

relations.subject: Concept
relations.note: Keyed by module path across this entire repo -- the only bounded context whose subject is the codebase itself rather than a runtime behaviour.

relations.subject: MCPToolMap
relations.note: Both are dispatch tables keyed by name, but route different protocols -- MCPToolMap wires MCP tool calls, HookDispatchTable wires Claude Code hook events -- no shared code path between them.

relations.subject: ToolDomainMap
relations.note: Used to describe a tool-hint row's origin in domain/skill terms; ToolScorer's own scoring does not depend on ToolDomainMap being populated (falls back to 'global'/empty skill when the personal registry is absent).
